note: 'frameworks' is the plan of record. 'implemented' is what actually exists and is what any runner attempts; a language with an empty list is skipped.

container.note: The Cloud Run container contract: listen on $PORT and speak HTTP. The same contract covers Fargate, ECS, EKS and plain Docker, so this host is not specific to one cloud.

gcp-func.note: Cloud Run functions. Gen2 functions are Cloud Run underneath, so the same code deployed as a Cloud Run container skips the Functions Framework entirely and runs on the container contract measured here.

lambda-rie.note: A genuinely different invocation model: no HTTP in the process, one invocation at a time, so it runs the serial suite rather than a rate ladder.

java:helidon-se.why: No first-party adapter for either function host, and no servlet to bridge. Same reason as vertx.

java:javalin.why: No first-party adapter for either function host. Javalin is a servlet on Jetty, so the generic servlet bridge would fit lambda-rie, but that shim is not written. Unwired rather than unable.

java:quarkus.why: lambda-rie: quarkus-amazon-lambda-http packages for the custom-runtime zip layout, not the lambda/java base image, so its rewritten netty-common is missing classes that layout supplies. gcp-func: quarkus-google-cloud-functions-http exists and is not wired yet. Unwired rather than unable on both.

java:spring-boot.why: spring-cloud-function-adapter-gcp routes to Function beans rather than to the @RestController the other two hosts serve, so measuring it would measure a different application. It runs on lambda-rie, where aws-serverless-java-container keeps the same controller.

java:vertx.why: No first-party adapter for either function host, and no servlet to bridge. A hand-written event-to-request shim would measure the shim rather than Vert.x.

node:koa.why: koa-bodyparser does not see the body through serverless-express, so the five body-carrying endpoints do not match. Unwired rather than unable: it conforms under gcp-func.
